mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% YoY signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to monetary tightening by the Federal Reserve, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY growth exceeds 2.5% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates strong labor market conditions, which is typically associated with economic expansion and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% YoY signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST declines by more than 10% YoY and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% MoM signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which is typically associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO increases by more than 1% MoM and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4%, it indicates a tight labor market and restrictive monetary policy, which historically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS > 2% and UNRATE < 4% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% MoM signals a weakening labor market, which is a leading indicator of economic contraction and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE increases by more than 0.5% MoM and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which is a strong indicator of economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS declines for three consecutive months and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth is negative for two consecutive quarters and industrial production (INDPRO) is also declining, it signals a supply-side recession, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 negative for 2 quarters and INDPRO declining
failure_condition: If GDPC1 is negative for two consecutive quarters and INDPRO is declining, but S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the cases, the hypothesis is rejected.
